summary: Racine's 1866 brick pier lighthouse at the Root River mouth, its 1839 shore predecessor, the 1903 Life-Saving station, and the keepers and rescues of Station No. 14.

structures.type: brick keeper's house with square tower (pier light)
structures.note: Lantern and deck removed 1901; tower capped with a hipped roof (LighthouseFriends)

structures.type: wooden framework pierhead beacon, painted white

facts.agency: Pugh Marina, per LighthouseFriends (the 1975 nomination named the U.S. Coast Guard as owner, then in litigation)

events.note: Work began on the conical brick shore light (Benjamin Pratt)
Shore light put into service; first keeper Amaziah Stebbins
Fifth-order Fresnel lens installed in the shore light
Brick keeper's house and tower completed on the north pier crib
Pier light activated 10 September 1866 with the fifth-order lens moved from the shore light
Fourth-order lens placed in the pier light's lantern (LighthouseFriends)
Shore light sold to L. S. Blake and James T. Elliott for $1,625
Wooden framework pierhead beacon, red light, activated 5 September
Shore light torn down by its owner; bricks used for a house on the site
Vessel ashore near Racine; Station No. 14 patrol reported it and set a watch; schooner Alleghany of Erie
Vessel grounded on a reef off Racine in heavy fog; torch not visible from Station No. 14
Station No. 14 crew rescued George Swift from drowning in Lake Michigan, 10 June
Sixth-order fixed red light re-established on the pierhead, 18 June 1896

LighthouseFriends gives 23 November 1901 as the date the pier light was discontinued. The Light-House Board's FY1901 report records the decision to discontinue it. The 1975 nomination dates the white light's removal to 1903
Metal pierhead tower with a fourth-order red light
Life-Saving station moved back from the river into a city street for temporary use while the channel was widened
Fixed white light removed from the 1866 tower to a steel tower on the pier end (nomination)
Two-story frame Life-Saving station and boathouse completed in 1903 (nomination). The 1904 report says new station buildings begun in the fiscal year 1903 had been completed and occupied at Racine
Racine Pierhead changed from fixed to flashing or occulting (acetylene)
Life-Saving Service merged into the Coast Guard (nomination's bracketed note)
Lighthouse became part of the adjacent Coast Guard station
Coast Guard station decommissioned; buildings now part of Pugh Marina
Added to the National Register of Historic Places (reference 75000077)

corrections.proposed: tower, brick, built 1866, standing (pier light); the 1837 date is the year Congress appropriated money for the first, shore light, which was built from 1838 and first lit in 1839
corrections.why: The standing brick tower on the pier was completed in 1866 (nomination; LighthouseFriends). The 1837 date belongs to the first light's appropriation, not to the surviving tower.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The record's 1837 date is Congress's appropriation for the first (shore) light. That light was begun in 1838 and first lit in 1839 (LighthouseFriends). The brick tower that stands today was completed on the pier in 1866 (nomination).

The 1865 discontinuance in the USLHS roster is of the shore light. Its fifth-order lens was moved to the pier light, activated 10 September 1866 (LighthouseFriends). The two stations are the same site, so the record's first light and its successor are being counted together.

notes_for_editor: Fact-check 2026-10-27. Changes made: (a) the 1904 Life-Saving report says the new station buildings begun in fiscal 1903 had been completed and occupied at Racine; the story no longer says they were completed in fiscal 1903 (the nomination dates completion to 1903); (b) the crib delay is split into the 1862 timber shortfall and the labour shortage to 1865, as LighthouseFriends gives them; (c) the 1880 station name is paraphrased (the report reads 'Station No. 14 (Racine, Wisconsin), Eleventh District'); (d) 'reported' replaces 'saw' for the 1880 patrol; (e) the 1901 Board quotation is shortened to 'decided to discontinue the pierhead light', because the OCR prints 'fourthorder'; (f) Pendergrast's 1837 words are attributed to LighthouseFriends, which quotes them; (g) the 1862 timber delay is sourced; (h) the sentence on the sex of Theresa W. Knudsen was removed from the story (the archive gives only a first name); the point stays here: the archive lists her as a first assistant in 1907 and LighthouseFriends prints Therse W. Knudsen; (i) the 1888 picket fence is paraphrased from LighthouseFriends. Still open: (1) The 1901 discontinuance is disputed: LighthouseFriends gives 23 November 1901, the Board's FY1901 report records the decision, and the 1975 nomination dates the white light's removal to 1903. Both dates are in the story. Record deactivated 1903 follows the nomination. (2) Brick colour: nomination says cream-coloured; LighthouseFriends and the USLHS place record say yellow. Both are stated. (3) Racine Harbor USLHS place record gives coordinates 43.2233, -88.2967, flagged suspect in the archive cache. They are not Racine's position; do not copy them. (4) Name collision, not linked: the Bulletins of 1913 and 1915 name an Edward W. Knudson as keeper of the Racine Reef light station, a different station; no source read connects him to this roster. (5) Theresa W. Knudsen's sex is inferred from the first name only and is not stated in the story. (6) The Life-Saving station's own keepers and surfmen are not named in the sources read. (7) OCR: the 1904 LSS sentence is garbled around 'Racine'; the quotation is the clean clause. The 1882 Swift rescue report is OCR-cut before 'small boat', so the story does not say the boat type. (8) The Journal-Times of 1 December 1903, quoted in the nomination, is not quoted in the story. (9) Pendergrast's 1837 report is read only through LighthouseFriends' quotation. (10) Storm-warning tower: described in 1975; its current status was not checked. (11) Pugh Marina ownership comes from LighthouseFriends alone; the nomination's 1975 owner, the Coast Guard, was in litigation then. No newer owner record was read. (12) No photos supplied.
